newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire may be flown home.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire may be flown home.

text.p: An airlift is among options being considered for repatriating Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees trapped in Zaire, a U.N. refugee agency spokesman said on Saturday.

"Some places would take over a week to reach by road from the border, so we are looking at how far west we can go and whether air repatriation is feasible," said Paul Stromberg, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Some 170,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees and former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen fled their largest camp in eastern Zaire at Tingi Tingi eight days ago before it fell to rebels.
A U.N. mission, made up of three aid agencies, intends to visit Tingi Tingi on Sunday to evaluate the needs of refugees.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has said hundreds of refugees are returning towards Tingi Tingi but Stromberg said UNHCR did not have a precise indication of to where the bulk of refugees scattered.
"The refugees are in an area three times the size of Switzerland and covered in forest. The only way to locate them will be to speak to people on the ground," said Stromberg.

Some reports indicate some headed along the main road towards northeastern Zaire's largest city of Kisangani, 250 km (150 miles) to the northwest of Tingi Tingi. But rebels are now closing in on the regional capital.
The U.N. World Food Programme said on Saturday hundreds of refugees had arrived at Ubundu town, 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Tingi Tingi, and food had arrived there by rail from Kisangani.

Before Tingi Tingi fell, UNHCR said it could not locate some 200,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees in eastern Zaire who fled their camps at the start of the rebellion by Tutsi rebels in October and November last year.
The refugees, along with 700,000 others who trekked home late last year, fled Rwanda in fear of reprisals for the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
